data.content_ref: inline:The target claims Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is 'defensible on his own terms' as a methodological rule. Yet the mechanism concedes that acting on such a theory 'requires a non-rational, pragmatic decision to treat the unrefuted as provisionally reliable.' Popper's framework is explicitly rationalist — he sought to ground the rationality of scientific method without induction. If the defense survives only by accepting a 'non-rational' pragmatic leap (as both the claim and mechanism acknowledge), then it is NOT defensible 'on his own terms' — it is defensible only by abandoning those rationalist terms. The artifact thus contradicts itself: it asserts the defense succeeds within Popper's framework while simultaneously conceding it succeeds only by leaving that framework. The claim's own qualifier — 'effectively costing the system any claim to rational assurance of success' — is not a caveat tacked onto the defense; it IS the failure of the defense on Popper's own terms. A defense that costs the system rational assurance cannot simultaneously be 'defensible' within a rationalist framework.
